moat_against: News Media (tabloids, print) in structural decline; print advertising eroding
Move/Realtor.com is #2 to Zillow in a frozen US housing-transaction market
Book publishing is hit-driven with no durable franchise economics
Australian and US housing-cycle exposure via REA and Move
Dual-class Murdoch control and a persistent conglomerate discount on the sum of the parts
moat_for: Dow Jones professional-information franchise: WSJ/Barron's digital subscriptions (6.26M digital-only across Dow Jones news products), enterprise/B2B now over half of segment profit, Risk & Compliance revenue +16% in FY26 to $392M — recurring data revenue with pricing power
REA Group: dominant Australian property portal with listing network effects (majority-owned, consolidated)
HarperCollins: #2 global trade publisher with a deep backlist
Scarce premium content is gaining AI-licensing value (OpenAI and Meta content deals)
moat_justification: A conglomerate average: Dow Jones (WSJ/Barron's, Risk & Compliance data) and REA Group's Australian portal are genuine franchises with pricing power and network effects, but News Media print is in structural decline, Move is #2 to Zillow, and book publishing is hit-driven. Consolidated returns are modest — owner's earnings of $650-734M on $8.5B of equity is high-single-digit — and the roic_proxy series is absent from fundamentals.json (no mergeable operating-income tag; the company reports segment EBITDA), so there is no evidence of through-cycle returns well above the cost of capital to justify 7+.
name: News Corporation
one_liner: Real franchises (Dow Jones, REA) inside a mediocre-return conglomerate, moat 5/10 — at $29.98 the $1.13 median-base OE/share yields only a 7.6% weighted IRR (weighted IV@15% $11.73); it clears 15% only at ~$11.73, so Tier D.
